subject: Banking
title: Decentralized Credit on Blockchain
description: A 60-second lesson on Decentralized Credit on Blockchain.

hook.text: DeFi lending platforms issue loans without banks or credit checks. A smart contract replaces the loan officer.

buildup.text: Borrowers post cryptocurrency as collateral. The smart contract automatically liquidates it if the loan-to-value ratio.

discovery.text: DeFi lending reached $50 billion in 2021. No credit score needed. Just collateral and code.

twist.text: DeFi requires over-collateralization. You need $150 in crypto to borrow $100.

climax.text: DeFi removed the bank but not the inequality. Lending without credit scores still requires assets most people don't.

punchline.text: No bank, no credit score, no bias. But you need $150 to borrow $100.

quiz.question: What is the main limitation of DeFi lending?
options: It requires over-collateralization, helping only those who already have assets

details.summary: Decentralized credit protocols on blockchain enable lending and borrowing without banks or credit checks by requiring borrowers to post cryptocurrency collateral. Smart contracts automate the entire process from origination to liquidation.
details.whyItMatters: DeFi lending challenges the fundamental model of credit scoring by replacing trust with collateral and code. It demonstrates that credit can function without intermediaries, though it currently only serves crypto-native borrowers.
takeaways: Borrowers post crypto collateral worth more than the loan amount
Smart contracts automatically liquidate collateral if values drop too far
No credit check, identity verification, or bank approval required

faq.question: Why would someone over-collateralize a loan?
faq.answer: Crypto holders borrow against their assets to access cash without selling and triggering taxable events. They maintain ownership and upside exposure while getting liquidity. The over-collateralization protects the lender without needing credit assessment.

faq.question: Can DeFi lending work for people without crypto assets?
faq.answer: Currently, no. The model requires collateral in the system. Under-collateralized DeFi lending exists experimentally through reputation systems and social collateral, but remains tiny compared to over-collateralized protocols.
